title: The 12th at Bletchingley: Baker Takes a Nine, Mullin Takes the Lot
title_candidates: The 12th at Bletchingley: Baker Takes a Nine, Mullin Takes the Lot
Twenty-Seven Shots in Eight Holes: How a Title Defence Dissolved in Surrey
No Bunkers, No Mercy, No Defence: Mullin's Record Week in East Sussex
Eagle at Eight, Sextuple at Twelve: Baker's Bletchingley
theme: Four brand-new courses flattered everybody — every man in the field posted his best Gross total ever — yet the Trophy was still settled by attrition: Baker held the outright lead on the second hole of the final round and lost it, and eight shots, in the most catastrophic eight-hole stretch of the tournament, while Mullin simply kept making pars and turned a scrap into the best Trophy score in TEG history.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck; affectionate ribbing of insiders, every number anchored in the data
opening_hook: Open on the par-3 12th at Bletchingley in R4 — SI 18, the easiest hole on the card — where Baker signs for a 9 (b10) and Mullin taps in a par to take the lead for the last time (b04); then loop back to Ashdown and explain how a 20-lead-change scrap ended up as a record.
foreshadow: The par-3 12th at Bletchingley — stroke index 18, the easiest hole in the tournament — will decide the Trophy
Baker arrives as defending champion (TEG 3) and leads after R1 by 3; the defence looks orderly
Mullin has back-to-back Jacket wins behind him and leads the Gross from R1 H11 onwards — the question is only how big it gets
Meller is the reigning double-Spoon holder and bottom of the pile after R1 and R3 — the Spoon appears to have a name on it already

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +9, by 8 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Ten routine lead changes at Ashdown while the field was bunched, then Mullin took over on R2 H13 and stretched to 16 clear after his +17 gross at Crowborough (b08, b09). Baker refused to go away — outright lead again on R4 H2 with a birdie on the SI-17 3rd hole... sorry, the 2nd (b03) — before Mullin drew level on H3 (b24) and Baker's 27-shot bleed from holes 9–16 (b05) ended it. Mullin's par on the 12th (b04) was the last change of the tournament, and +9 is the best Trophy total in TEG history to date (b01).

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +81, by 19 from Stuart Neumann)
competitions.how: Effectively over by lunchtime on day one: Mullin took the Gross lead at Ashdown's 11th and was never headed across the remaining 62 holes, the four lead changes all coming while the card was still half-empty. 23, 22, 17, 19 — the 17 at Crowborough (b08) the second-best Gross round in TEG history — for +81, the best Gross total ever recorded in a TEG, and a third consecutive Jacket (b02).

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: A slow-motion accident: 3rd, 3rd, 4th, 5th. Williams was already leaking at Ashdown (22 shots gone over the closing nine, b12), lost 18 in six holes at Crowborough (b30), then went to the bottom for good in R4 — quads at the 5th and 6th (b19), triple at the 13th (b21) and 16 shots surrendered over the last six (b23) for his worst round to date in both net and gross (b33, b34). Meller, twice the reigning Spoon holder, occupied last place in R1, R3 and briefly on R4 H11 after a 10 (b20, b27) and still got out alive.

rounds.chosen_headline: Eagle at Eight, Nine at Twelve: Baker's 27-Shot Unravelling
rounds.angle: Bletchingley's fast parkland gives Baker the outright lead on H2 and an eagle at the 8th, then takes 27 shots off him in eight holes — sextuples at the SI-18 12th and the 15th — while Mullin's three pars at the SI-3/SI-1/13 stretch and a par at the 12th convert a scrap into records; Williams' closing collapse hands over the Spoon.

players.arc: Runner-up in TEG 3 and holder of back-to-back Jackets, he leads the Gross from Ashdown's 11th to the final green, posts the second-best Gross round in TEG history at Crowborough, and rides out Baker's R4 charge to claim both the best Trophy total (+9) and the best Gross total (+81) TEG has seen.

The defending champion leads after R1, is level at Bletchingley's 3rd, eagles the 8th — and then loses 27 shots in eight holes, including sextuple bogeys at the 12th and 15th, to finish 8 back with a personal-best Gross total (+113) that will be no consolation whatsoever.
Third, third, fourth, fifth: a steady erosion that ends with his worst round to date (+15, +43 gross) and the Wooden Spoon, achieved in the same tournament as his best-ever Gross total (+152).

Reigning double-Spoon holder who produces the worst hole in TEG history (a 12 at Ashdown's 11th), sits bottom after R1 and R3, takes two 10s in the final round — and still escapes the Spoon while recording his best Gross total (+107).
Jacket runner-up 19 adrift with a personal-best +100 Gross, and a brief resident of last place in R2 and at Crowborough's 2nd before quietly steadying.

venue_notes: TEG's first visit to East Sussex (and the Surrey borders) — and all four courses new to everyone, so treat the venues as characters rather than as history: Royal Ashdown Forest's bunkerless heathland high above sea level in R1 (where Meller's 12 needed no sand at all), Harvey Jarrett's mature Lingfield parkland with its grand trees and water in R2, Crowborough Beacon's MacKenzie holes and South Downs panoramas in R3 (backdrop to Mullin's 88), and Paul Wright's modern, fast-draining Bletchingley in R4, where undulating parkland and a short 12th decided all three competitions.
course_history_notes: Every round of TEG 4 was a first visit for all five players — no course history existed anywhere in the field, so nobody had an excuse or a benchmark.

Unfamiliar ground flattered the whole field: personal-best Gross totals for Williams (+152, b13), Meller (+107, b14), Baker (+113, b15) and Neumann (+100, b16), and an all-time TEG-best +81 for Mullin (b02).
Mullin's four cards — 91 Ashdown, 94 Lingfield, 88 Crowborough, 91 Bletchingley — set the opening course marks at all four venues.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R4 H12 at Bletchingley — Baker's 9 on the par-3 SI-18 12th against Mullin's routine par (b10, b04); the outright lead changed hands for the last time and the 8-shot margin was built from there.
Green Jacket: R1 H11 at Ashdown — Mullin took the Gross lead and was never headed over the remaining 62 holes, the cushion growing 3 → 7 → 16 → 19 (b02).

Wooden Spoon: R4 H13 at Bletchingley — Williams's triple bogey dropped him to the bottom for the final time (b21), the start of a 16-shot slide over the closing six holes (b23) that let Meller off the hook.
